problems.title: Annulus from sums and differences
problems.question: Two concentric circles have diameter sum 2 and circumference difference 1. Find the annulus area.
problems.idea: Factor the difference of the squared radii.
steps: The diameter condition gives R+r=1.
The circumference condition gives R-r=1/(2π).

problems.title: A cubic and its inverse
problems.question: Draw y=x³ and y=∛x and solve x³≤∛x.
problems.idea: Cubing preserves inequalities on the whole real line.
steps: The graphs are reflections in y=x and intersect at (-1,-1),(0,0),(1,1).
The expression changes sign only at -1,0,1. Testing the four intervals gives x≤-1 or 0≤x≤1.
Include all three intersection inputs because the inequality allows equality.

problems.title: Horizontal chords of a parabola
problems.question: The lines y=3 and y=15 cut y=x²-6x+8. Find the area of the quadrilateral between the chords.
problems.idea: Complete the square to find the chord endpoints.
steps: At y=3, x=1,5, so the lower chord is 4.
At y=15, x=-1,7, so the upper chord is 8. The height is 12.
The convex trapezoid area is (4+8)·12/2=72.
problems.note: The answer uses the convex quadrilateral determined by the four points; listing vertices in crossing order would not describe that region.

problems.title: Integer points of a rational graph
problems.question: Find all integer-coordinate points on y=(4x-5)/(2x-1).
steps: For integer x, the odd number 2x-1 must divide 3.
Its possible values are -3,-1,1,3, giving x=-1,0,1,2.
Substitute to obtain y=3,5,-1,1 respectively.

problems.title: Half a regular hexagon
problems.question: In the pictured right triangle, four vertices of a regular hexagon lie on its sides. The shorter triangle leg is 2 dm. Find the common area.
problems.idea: The sloping triangle side joins opposite hexagon vertices.
formulas: Regular hexagon area=6(√3s²/4); its horizontal vertex spacing gives triangle base=3s/2.
steps: Let s be the hexagon side. The drawn horizontal short leg spans 3s/2, so s=4/3 dm.
The diagonal on the hypotenuse divides the hexagon into two equal halves, and one half lies inside the triangle.

problems.title: An inequality involving a composition
problems.question: For f(x)=(2x-1)/(x+1), solve f(f(x))≤x.
problems.idea: Check both the original function and composition domains.
steps: The inequality becomes (x²-x+1)/x≥0.
The numerator is (x-1/2)²+3/4, always positive.
Thus x>0; these inputs also satisfy every original restriction.

problems.title: A cube-root cancellation
problems.question: Simplify (( (1/a-a)/[(∛a+∛(1/a)+1)(∛a+∛(1/a)-1)] )+∛a)^(-3).
steps: The large fraction is u⁻¹-u.
Adding u leaves u⁻¹, which is nonzero.
Raising to power -3 gives u³=a. The denominator u²+1+u⁻² is positive.

problems.title: Subtract two circular segments
problems.question: Circles have as diameters the legs 1,√3 and hypotenuse of the drawn right triangle. Find the grey region inside the hypotenuse circle and outside both leg circles.
problems.idea: Subtract the two leg-circle caps from the outer hypotenuse semicircle.
steps: The triangle angles are 30°,60°,90°. The hypotenuse circle has radius 1, so its semicircle away from the right-angle vertex has area π/2.
The larger leg circle has radius √3/2. Its cap on that side of the hypotenuse has central angle 120°=2π/3 and area π/4-3√3/16.
The smaller leg circle has radius 1/2. Its cap has central angle 60°=π/3 and area π/24-√3/16. The two caps meet at the altitude foot without overlapping interiors.

problems.title: A telescoping correction to a constant
problems.question: Sum the first 199 terms of aₖ=(-k²-k+1)/(k(k+1)).
problems.idea: Split the fraction into a constant and a telescoping difference.
steps: The 199 constant terms sum to -199.
The remaining differences cancel to 1-1/200=199/200.

problems.title: Add square roots of similar areas
problems.question: Four triangles with sides parallel to the large triangle’s sides have areas 1,16,4,9 and bases partitioning its base. Find the large area.
problems.idea: Similar-triangle areas are proportional to squared side lengths.
formulas: If large area is S, a small base/large base=√(small area/S).
steps: The four base fractions sum to 1.
Hence √S=10 and S=100.
